Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: English promotional architecture poster for eylema.dev, replacing its v0.5 poster.
Edit target: supplied older EylemA poster. Completely redesign its diagram for architecture v0.7; retain only the exact EylemA wordmark, orange E icon, palette and premium technical illustration style. Do not retain the old topology or version.
Make one polished wide landscape 16:9 infographic, high-resolution, with generous whitespace and readable text. Off-white paper #F7F6F2, ink #17252B, orange #EE5638. Shallow isometric white/graphite modules with restrained orange accents, clean sans-serif labels. The diagram is informative and presentation-ready, not a UI screenshot. No tiny paragraphs, no extraneous decorative objects.
Header: existing EylemA wordmark left; headline "Human ideas. Composable systems." and pill "ARCHITECTURE · v0.7".
At top a human governance bar "Human goals · authority · budgets · corrections". Under it a thin permissions line "Separate permissions: execute · collect · train · external disclosure · ecosystem export". Human governance constrains the platform; model suggestions do not grant permissions.
Main operating band across the middle, left to right:
1 "Jobs & contracts" with a typed-flow document icon.
2 A wide panel "OPTIONAL MODEL ROLES" with exactly nine equal labeled tiles in a 3x3 matrix:
row1 "Perception", "Reasoning", "Planning";
row2 "Decision", "Action policy", "World model";
row3 "Specialist", "Critic", "Representation".
Within this panel underneath the tiles: "Choose roles per job · compatible profiles". Do not imply nine mandatory models or simultaneous residency. World model is optional like all others. Representation includes retrieval; Decision and Action policy must remain distinct.
3 "Tools & skills" with bounded tool/package icons.
4 "Rust authority" with an orange-accented execution core and subtitle "Validate · execute · journal".
5 "Observed outcomes" with evidence/receipt icon.
Orange main arrows go Jobs & contracts -> optional model roles -> tools & skills -> Rust authority -> observed outcomes. A single solid observed-feedback return from observed outcomes to Jobs & contracts is captioned "Observe → compare → correct". These are conceptual proposed integration connections, not installed runtime.
A discreet note near operating band: "Workflow: XState · proposed; Rust retains authority".
Below roles, two restrained deployment chips: "Local-only: no hosted fallback" and "External models: explicit configuration + permission".
Below the operating band, a left support module around one third width titled "PROJECT KNOWLEDGE & MEMORY". It contains an orange rightward source-flow "Permitted sources → RAG / recall → Context", and six small clearly labeled memory-kind chips:
"Working", "Episodic", "Semantic", "Procedural", "Knowledge graph", "Analytical".
Its exact short scope notes: "Rights · lineage · expiry rechecked" and "Integrated retrieval: acceptance pending".
One fine connector from its Context output goes upward only to the model-role panel as role context. Do not connect retrieval context straight to execution or grant authority. Do not put database product logos or imply accepted graph/vector/analytical engines.
To the right of knowledge module, a visually separate improvement module titled "PERMITTED IMPROVEMENT · PLANNED".
Left-to-right flow of five modules:
"Permitted episodes" -> "Curated data" -> "Native Rust training" (subtitle "Planned · LoRA / QLoRA") -> "Held-out evaluation" -> "Human-controlled promotion".
One dashed connector from promotion goes back to model assignments / skill packages, with caption "Accepted profiles / skills". It must not point to Rust authority or replace observed evidence. Collection and training remain distinct from executing a job.
Short external-reference note below training: "External recipes: separate reference / export gates". Do not show Unsloth as the native production training engine; native gradients and LoRA/QLoRA are planned per model.
Footer separated by fine rule:
"Scoped foundation: task console · contracts · source context · counter tools / skills"
"Primary target: Apple M4 Pro · macOS"
"Integrated model / RAG / training acceptance pending"
"Illustration is not execution or performance evidence."
"eylema.dev".
Hierarchy: large headline, distinct operating/knowledge/improvement sections, medium text labels, clear factual scope footer. Every listed label must be accurate, spelled correctly and visible. Connectors must be unambiguous and avoid running through text. No model brands/download counts, no performance numbers, no Linux deployment, no database-installed claims, no green completion badges, no proof of universal model support. Keep all content comfortably inside safe margins.
